flow.zh: --  霧是她的面具，鴿子是她的披風

en: What is wide is the street
Narrow is the alley
What brushes past is a hutong alley
Turning through the hutong
Turning into a narrow lane
Merging into the flow of people on the street
Streets and waterways, crisscrossing
Strolling along the street, the waterway runs crosswise
Riding a boat along the waterway, the streets run lengthwise
What flows through the streets is people
What flows in the waterway is a boat

zh: 是鴿子劃過的聖馬可廣場
en: Waterway begets waterway
Street spreads into street
Waterways and streets, branching in every direction
A map is superfluous
No need to set the goal in advance
Round the corner is the Bridge of Sighs
Looking across the street
It is Piazza San Marco, streaked by the flight of pigeons
Waterways wide and narrow
The splendid, resplendent gondola
Song winding round and round
This ancient city, like a mirage
Telling what kind of history
What kind of story has been passed down
Small river, small bridge, rippling in each other's reflection
Narrow streets and lanes, bustling with people coming and going
Small shops and stalls, varied and colorful
Letting the lamplight kindle the dusk
Thin mist sways the shadow of the oar
Bringing back only a few short lines
Writing of a floating city of water
Recording a traveler's impression

points.zh: 聖馬可廣場和嘆息橋是威尼斯的主要地標。聖馬可廣場 (Piazza San Marco ) 以及其大教堂總是擠滿來自世界各地的旅客，也是旅客歸去後，對於威尼斯所留下的深刻記憶。馬可是耶穌的門徒，聖經馬可福音書的作者，威尼斯人奉他為護城聖者。相傳兩個威尼斯商人，從埃及亞歷山大把馬聖徒馬可遺骨偷運到威尼斯，并於同年為聖馬可興建教堂。堂內有馬可陵墓，大教堂以聖馬可命名，教堂前面的廣場也得名為聖馬可廣場。19世紀拿破崙贊稱之為「歐洲最美的客廳」。廣埸上最令人驚奇的景象，是密密麻麻的鴿子，安靜時，逐步啄食，驚動時，舉翅齊飛，掩遮廣埸天空，有若掀動的披風，十分壯觀。有謂無鴿不成廣場，是歐洲城市的特色，以聖馬可廣場為最。
points.en: St. Mark's Square and the Bridge of Sighs are the principal landmarks of Venice. St. Mark's Square (Piazza San Marco) and its basilica are always crowded with visitors from all over the world, and it is what travelers remember most vividly of Venice after they return home. Mark was a disciple of Jesus and the author of the Gospel of Mark; the people of Venice revere him as the city's patron saint. According to legend, two Venetian merchants smuggled the relics of St. Mark out of Alexandria, Egypt, to Venice, and a church for St. Mark was built that same year. The basilica houses Mark's tomb, is named after him, and the square in front of it likewise takes its name from him. In the 19th century, Napoleon praised it as "the finest drawing room in Europe." The most astonishing sight in the square is its dense flocks of pigeons — when undisturbed they peck about steadily, but when startled they take flight all at once, filling the sky over the square like a great cloak unfurling, a truly spectacular sight. It is said that no piazza is complete without pigeons, a feature distinctive to European cities, and St. Mark's Square is the foremost example.

points.zh:
**  嘆息橋 ( Bridge of Sighs ) 是白色大理石打造的巴洛克風格建築，方形雕花窗口，頂部穹隆覆蓋，形成二道優美的弧度，像一幅橫跨水面的雕刻圖案。橋的一端是當年的總督府和法院，另一端是關押死囚的監獄。嘆息橋建於1602年，正逢意大利文藝復興之際，也是威尼斯共和國鼎盛繁榮，面具狂歡和貢多拉 (gondola) 盛行的時代。在這樣一個雍容華麗的時代，人文浪漫的水城，最絕望的是死牢裡的囚犯，最痛苦的是剛被判死罪的人。從法院押往死牢的路，就是這座嘆息橋，一座橋下貢多拉搖搖晃晃，歌聲繚繚繞繞的橋。短短的橋，小小的窗，讓死囚在押入黑牢前，對外面光燦的世界，飄浮的水城，做最後一瞥，陽光和自由成為來世的渴望。生命最後的一瞥能不嘆息嗎 ?  據傳嘆息橋名稱的由來，是源自英國詩人拜倫在1812所寫的詩 : “ Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage“ 的第一節 :
“  I stood in Venice,  on the Bridge of Sighs.
A palace and a prison on each hand.
I saw from out the wave of her structures rise
As from the stroke of the enchanter’s wand.“
